content: Synthetic camphor, menthol, and methyl salicylate plaster is an FDA-approved external analgesic used for the treatment of simple backache, arthritis, strains, bruises, and sprains. Common adverse reactions include seizures, nausea, vomiting, warmth, headache, confusion, vertigo, delirium, hallucinations, tremors, and contact eczema. Adult Indications and Dosage Indications: This plaster is indicated for the temporary relief of minor aches and pains in muscles and joints caused by simple backache, arthritis, strains, bruises, and sprains. Dosage: Clean the affected area and remove the paper film from the plaster. Adults should apply one plaster to the affected area no more than 3 to 4 times daily. For children under 12 years of age, this product should not be used without consulting a physician, as improper use may be dangerous. Pediatric Indications and Dosage Indications: Similar to adults, this plaster is indicated for the temporary relief of minor aches and pains in muscles and joints due to simple backache, arthritis, strains, bruises, and sprains. Dosage: For children 12 years and older, apply one plaster to the affected area no more than 3 to 4 times daily. For children under 12 years, do not use this product without consulting a physician. Contraindications There is limited information regarding contraindications for this plaster in the drug label. Warnings For external use only. Allergy Alert: This product contains natural rubber latex, which may cause allergic reactions. Adverse Reactions Postmarketing Experience: Reported adverse reactions include seizures, nausea, vomiting, warmth, headache, confusion, vertigo, delirium, hallucinations, tremors, elevated lactate dehydrogenase, elevated aspartate aminotransferase-to-alanine aminotransferase ratio, and contact eczema. Drug Interactions There is limited information regarding drug interactions for this plaster in the drug label. Use in Specific Populations Pregnancy: There is no FDA or Australian guidance on the use of this plaster in pregnant women. Labor and Delivery: No FDA guidance is available for use during labor and delivery. Nursing Mothers: No FDA guidance is available for use in nursing mothers. Pediatric Use: No FDA guidance is available for use in pediatric settings. Geriatric Use: No FDA guidance is available for use in geriatric settings. Gender and Race: No specific FDA guidance is available regarding use in gender or racial populations. Renal and Hepatic Impairment: No FDA guidance is available for use in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. Females of Reproductive Potential and Males: No FDA guidance is available for use in these populations. Immunocompromised Patients: No FDA guidance is available for use in immunocompromised patients. Administration and Monitoring Administration: This product is for external application only. Monitoring: There is limited information regarding monitoring requirements in the drug label. Overdosage There is limited information regarding overdosage of this plaster. In case of suspected drug poisoning or overdose, contact the National Poison Help hotline (1-800-222-1222) immediately. Storage Keep the product in a tightly closed container. Store at room temperature (15º to 30ºC or 59º to 86ºF) and away from sunlight. Patient Counseling Information Do Not Use: On irritated or damaged skin. On wounds. With a heating pad. If pregnant or nursing. In any manner other than as directed. When Using: Avoid contact with eyes or mucous membranes. Do not bandage tightly. Stop Use and Consult a Doctor If: The condition worsens. Symptoms persist for more than 7 days. Symptoms clear up and return within a few days. Excessive skin irritation develops. Nausea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, diarrhea, or skin rash occurs. For arthritis pain, if pain persists for more than 10 days, redness is present, or the condition affects children under 12 years of age. Precautions with Alcohol The interaction between alcohol and this plaster has not been established. Consult your doctor regarding the effects of alcohol consumption while using this medication. Brand Names This product is marketed under the brand name 701 Dieda Zhengtong Yaogao Medicated Plaster. Look-Alike Drug Names There is limited information regarding look-alike drug names for this plaster in the drug label.
